— Frequently asked questions

Good questions.
Clearer expectations.

A few practical answers before discussing your business, website, or marketing project.

Where should we start?+

Start with the business goal and the issue you want to solve. A review can identify whether the priority is the website, search visibility, advertising, measurement, or a combination. The scope is agreed before implementation.

Can we work on one specific service?+

Yes. An engagement can focus on one area, such as an SEO audit, a website project, campaign planning, or measurement. Related work is recommended when it addresses a real dependency, with scope discussed separately.

What should I prepare for a project discussion?+

A short explanation of your business, website URL, goals, current challenges, and any known constraints is useful. Do not send passwords, customer records, or other sensitive information through the inquiry form.

Do you guarantee rankings, leads, or revenue?+

No. Search engines, auctions, customer demand, budgets, and implementation all affect results. I focus on sound work, clear measurement, and informed recommendations without promising a particular commercial outcome.

How are scope and costs agreed?+

The requirements, deliverables, responsibilities, timing, and any third-party costs should be discussed and documented before work begins. There is no universal package price published because requirements differ.

Can you work with my existing website or team?+

An initial review can establish what is possible on the current platform and how work would be coordinated. Access requirements, implementation ownership, and dependencies are agreed as part of the scope.

— A conversation is a good place to start
